claims.claim: A University of Florida study of more than 1,100 participants found repeated forced smiles erased mood benefits or reversed them.
claims.episode_span: More than 1,100 participants completed tasks that required them to smile either once or repeatedly under controlled conditions. A single artificial smile produced a small positive shift in self-reported mood. Repeating the action erased the benefit or reversed it, leaving participants feeling worse than at baseline.
claims.source_title: Forcing yourself to smile can actually make you miserable
claims.supporting_quote: In a University of Florida study involving more than 1,100 participants, researchers discovered that while a single artificial smile can provide a small mood boost, repeatedly faking smiles can erase that benefit or even reverse it.
